gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: I'll tell you everything ___ you promise to keep it between us.
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' sets the condition attached to the promise.

gaps.sentence: The flight was cheap ___ it landed at 4 a.m.
gaps.explanation: 'Although' introduces a full clause; 'despite/in spite' need noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: The flat is spacious and well located; ___, the rent is surprisingly low.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds another supporting point in the same direction.

gaps.sentence: She has decided to cycle to work ___ taking the bus.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + -ing' = in place of the bus journey.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: It was pouring with rain. ___, the open-air concert went ahead.
gaps.explanation: The concert happened despite the rain: Nevertheless is concessive.

gaps.sentence: We went for a long walk ___ it was drizzling.
gaps.explanation: Only the conjunction 'even though' can introduce the finite clause 'it was drizzling'.
